::: {#thm-composition-graph}
#### The graph of a composition is a composition of graphs

Let $g : A \to B$ and $f : B \to C$ be functions (@def-function),
and write $\Gamma_f$ for the graph (@def-graph) of $f$.
Then the graph of the composition $f \circ g$ (@def-composition) is the composition of relations (@def-relation-composition)

$$
\Gamma_{f \circ g} = \Gamma_f \circ \Gamma_g.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Let $a \in A$ and $c \in C$.
By the definition of composition of relations,
$(a, c) \in \Gamma_f \circ \Gamma_g$ exactly when some $b \in B$ has $(a, b) \in \Gamma_g$ and $(b, c) \in \Gamma_f$,
that is, $b = g(a)$ and $c = f(b)$.
Only $b = g(a)$ can work,
so this holds exactly when $c = f(g(a)) = (f \circ g)(a)$,
which is when $(a, c) \in \Gamma_{f \circ g}$.

:::

:::
